The roll burns: nobody can prove what anyone owes; the gang scatters on the shore, and MQ03 decides whether their months stand. Three places within a day change: the camp (the cutting withdrawn, the clutch grey, the uxith dark), the barge (the crew parent off), the paddies behind the camp (the families on the shore).

The Owing roll (labour-and-bondage §2): the debt is months owed, with months added for food; the holder is a Lilmoth debt-labour broker who bought the gang's months from earlier holders (drift 2, transferable) and hires it to Hereguard Plantation; the overseer reads the roll; the exit in law is working the months off, and in practice the food months outrun the work, so the gang families are born into it. The bound want to be home under their own Hist, and have the right to refuse help: the washed-out woman will not leave the gang while her daughter owes.
none the player can stop: the cell cuts the roots at dusk as the player is at the fire; the player can only choose which one of the three witnesses lives

Two of the gang are visibly washed out from years away from their Hist, and their cutting is cut; the player's own line is blank, so no amount of work can pay it down. Whoever the player does not reach in the burning camp dies, and the gang families lose their clutch.

The cutting's withdrawal: the light in the cutting goes out, the sap stops, the uxith goes dark, in front of the gang families, with the harvest at its roots as the officiant and the severed clutch as the sign.

e-mine: the player's months are released: the hurt who lived go with the broker's skiff to Soulrest at dawn and the mats stand empty; the broker is back at the Lilmoth dock and civil; the house's door is the player's (the safehouse); Lilmoth cools a little to a stranger who ended a broker's claim with coin from somewhere unnamed. e-theirs: the survivor walks out of Lilmoth by the shore road (a placed actor), the broker at the dock still holds the player's line and the dock's pilots ask a high passage of a hand under it (setPrice service.lilmoth.dock-passage), Nesh-Deeka calls the player a kind fool and gives half the purse, Lilmoth warms. e-no-release: the hurt go with the skiff and the player's claim with them, the dock asks the same passage; the Reed holds back the purse and thinks the less of the player, Lilmoth is easy with a player who gave a trader no offence. e-broker-dead: the broker is dead in a trader's house, nobody holds the player's line, the Reed pays no purse for a killing in its house and thinks the less of the player, Lilmoth cools to the player (the engine's own murder response stands: witnesses, the guard bounty). e-nesh-dead: Salts-The-Catch keeps the house alone and shuts the door to the player; the woman who kept the strangers' boat left word at it. e-both-dead: neither is left and Salts-The-Catch wants the player gone. The same four with a refused coin (96 to 99) give no rank, no purse and no Reed standing; the player keeps Nesh-Deeka's word that she will not hand the player back as her own favour and the house door stays hers. In each the broker's topic at the dock changes (topic.mq03-broker-after) or Salts-The-Catch's at the house (topic.mq03-house-after); one standing moves, three places change (the house door, the dock, the road) and one thing becomes impossible (the survivor's release or the player's).

The Owing (labour-and-bondage §2): the debt is months owed and months added for food, held by a Lilmoth debt-labour broker who bought them from earlier holders (drift 2) and hires the gang out (QA7). The roll is burnt, so the months stand only on the word of those who heard them read; the exit in law is a release the holder speaks before witnesses, or the months worked off; the exit in practice is the broker's price. The bound want to go home under their own Hist and may refuse help: the survivor will not swear falsely that the months were never read, and Finds-The-Other-Bank will not swear to months on a line she heard read blank nor leave while her daughter owes; an open claim shuts Lilmoth's dock to the bound hand, as a berth is bought with somebody's months (labour §3).

A survivor who will not swear to a figure bears the broker's spite at the next hire (e-mine and e-no-release take whoever lived to Soulrest in the skiff); a release for the player is a release not given to the survivor; the families' months stand in every ending, because the broker frees one hand's months for one price and no more; Finds-The-Other-Bank stays bound for her daughter's sake in e-theirs as in the rest; in e-broker-dead the families' months pass with the broker's estate to Wuleen-Sei and the barge at Soulrest, who hold them as he did, so the dead man frees no one.

the broker's skiff leaves for Soulrest at the first dawn after he sits down to bargain (said by the broker and by Salts-The-Catch); stage 40 starts a timer ev.mq03.skiff and the world sets the deadline: daysSince is a world-time day count, true from the first midnight after the start, so with timeOfDay dawn it fires at the first dawn after the next midnight (a player who sits down before dawn gets that day too), or two days at the latest, when the stage's fail-forward takes the player into the dream as soon as they stand in the house (zone.mq03.house), the broker's parent turned off (the skiff has gone) and the release topics ended with stage 40; a player outside the house at dawn is not moved, the dream waits at the threshold. Nothing before stage 40 has a clock, so no path skips Nesh-Deeka's terms or the taste. It is a trader's dawn, not the quest's clock: a player who misses it loses only the release (e-no-release is a full ending and MQ04 follows), so the main quest's no-timer rule holds.
